Tech Report: Happy Thanksgiving (From Me To You)

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1166 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Stylebyemilyhenderson

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I just wanted to pop in and say thank you all so much for being here.
  • Recent findings suggest that daily content is such a fun wild ride, y’all.
  • In a recent development, anyway, I just really, really want you to feel my appreciation and gratitude for you reading today.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I just wanted to pop in and say thank you all so much for being here. Whether you pop in every morning, once a week/month, or just once a year, I’m just so grateful to still be doing this job with my team for you (and us). There is no perfect job, life, city, spouse, school, etc., but the list of what I love about this job and blog is so long, and absolutely dominates the “harder stuff” column. Sure, the years where we are panicking about social media, TikTok, and now AI can feel scary, but the fact that you are still here is what matters, and the latest challenges are actually exciting. There are so few of us left running daily design blogs, and I have to give credit to you all and my team for showing up every day. I hope to be doing this till the day I die, decades from now, but I can’t without the both of you.

Recent findings suggest that daily content is such a fun wild ride, y’all. We are constantly trying upcoming things, some that work and some that don’t, and it’s all with the goal of creating a space for a few minutes in your day that you find enjoyable. That’s kinda it. Sure, we want to educate, inspire, and entertain, but only in the name of making people feel good or just slightly better than before. Following the enthusiasm of others has always been one of my driving forces in life (I’m an Enneagram 7 and was raised Mormon, so perhaps positivity is in my blood), and creating blog posts that you find enjoyable or helpful in any way is the most fun daily challenge.

In a recent development, anyway, I just really, really want you to feel my appreciation and gratitude for you reading today. Without you here, we wouldn’t be here either. And I don’t take that for granted, ever. I am SO driven to keep doing this – writing, designing, producing, sharing – as long as you’ll have us and I can tell it’s adding value to the world. Every comment really means something to us. THANK YOU.

Sources indicate that A huge thanks to Jess, Caitlin, Gretchen, Mallory and Marlee for being the literal dream team. Sure, it’s my name and face, but the amount of experience, expertise, creativity, and hard work that goes into every single post on all platforms is so intense, you guys. And these ladies are the absolute best in the world, and I’m so grateful that every day they are still here.

Sources indicate that thank you. Thank you. Thank you.

My sincere thanks to all of you at Team EHD. I’ve followed since Design Star days and look forward to checking in every morning. Grateful to you all!

In a recent development, thank you so much KHD. I honestly means the world to us that you’ve been with us for so long (so many changes). Thank you thank you thank you. xx.

Sources indicate that I love starting my day with the EHD team. Thankful for you all!

Recent findings suggest that thank YOU, Kim. The long term, daily readers honestly keep us here. I feel just so grateful to still be here (I can’t say it enough, apparently) and that’s because of you. Thank you thank you. xx.

Thank YOU EHD! Every morning I pour my coffee, grab my computer, read your blog, and have a little quiet time before I start my day. I look forward to it! I enjoy all the posts. I love design and you all have inspired me so much. Happy Thanksgiving to you all!

Thank you, Chris! Its just so nice to hear that we are a part of your day. And I so appreciate you taking the time to tell us. On the days that I have a lot of self-doubt, these comments really help, I can’t even tell you. xx.

Industry observers note that thank you for all you do to bring fun and positivity to the world. I’ve been reading since the early LA days- when you were pregnant with Charlie! So happy you are here. Keep up the great work and have a lovely holiday.

Sources indicate that thirteen years!!!! Thank you thank you thank you. I feel like you’ve really watched me grow up. The version of myself with babies feels like yesterday and also soooo long ago (being in your late 40’s is weird, y’all, i feel 27). Anyway, thank you thank you. xx.

Recent findings suggest that ahh did i miss arlyn leaving? i love her posts!

Recent findings suggest that I’m pretty sure she’s considered a ‘contributor’ but not part of the daily and strategic functioning of EHD. I love her posts too! She brings another level of ‘real life’ design and a good eye.

Recent findings suggest that arlyn is a freelance contributor, paid per post!! But I should absolutely include her (she used to be full time and I have so much trust in her). She’s not involved in running the business, per say, and isn’t on calls with us, but her writing, creativity and expertise adds so much to the posts that she writes. No one gets the world of digital media and design like her.

Industry observers note that thank you for doing what you all do! It really does bring a dose of inspiration and levity each day, particularly as I’m dealing with a very bureaucratic day job. I love popping by your site on my lunch break to tickle the right side of my brain a bit. I am inspired by how adaptable and transparent you all are, and how you aren’t afraid to try newly introduced things. I am especially grateful for how you’ve helped me decorate and love my rental 💚 Happy Thanksgiving 🦃!

Thank you thank you thank you. That is so nice to hear. Literally all I need to know – that we are a quick dose of happiness during someones day. Thank you so much for telling us and taking the time to write it here. Its going in my mental bank when I need it. Happy thanksgiving Caitlin. xx.

Recent findings suggest that the daily posts are a breath of fresh air each morning. Thank you!

It has been revealed that thank you so much. It means so much to hear it (I promise, digital media is a scary place at times, this blog full of nice daily readers still feels safe to me). xx.

Sources indicate that I rarely comment, but I read every post. Your blog is truly a bright spot on the internet! Thank you.

This is my first and favourite stop every morning! Thanks, EHD team! So grateful to have this to look forward to every day! Happy Thanksgiving from Canada xx.

Thank you so much for saying that, Kristyn. Hearing that will never get old, I swear. xx.

#234. Industry News: Faux Brass Botanical Air Dry Clay Ornaments

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (576 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jenniferrizzo ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Faux Brass Botanical Air Dry Clay Ornaments

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (576 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jenniferrizzo

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There is something about brass that has a timeless quality to it.
  • (This post contains affiliate links, see our affiliate and sponsor disclosure here.).
  • -Faux or real non-toxic pine plant branches or twigs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There is something about brass that has a timeless quality to it. This project made with air dry clay will have people wondering if these ornaments real metal! We used air dry clay, metallic paint and real pine branch sprigs  to create these faux brass botanical ornaments. They look almost like real metal and the plant impressions have a pretty natural look almost like they were molded or cast that way. This project can also be switched up by changing the paint finish to silver or even copper. This air dry clay ornament project will take about an hour of creative time to make the first part, overnight time for the clay to dry, and then about an hour of painting time to complete the rest.

(This post contains affiliate links, see our affiliate and sponsor disclosure here.).

-Dedicated clay rolling pin or dowel rod.

-Faux or real non-toxic pine plant branches or twigs.

-Antique Gold, Bronze or Brass metallic craft paint.

-Small stick or straw to make a hole in the ornament.

You can find the supplies here an Amazon for this project.

Here’s a tip when working with clay: use parchment paper under clay to make it easier to move and flip while drying.

For my botanical impression, I used small sprigs from my Alaskan Cedar, and my Scotch Pine. Any evergreen or branch that has stiff and retains needles will work. I liked the Alaskan Cedar, because it has small berry-like pine cones that I knew would look cool. When using fresh greenery, make sure you always know what you are picking. Some evergreen look a likes can be toxic.

While the clay is still wet, press the branches into the clay. Rolling a dowel rod across the clay and branch helps to apply even pressure and create a nice, deep impression. After rolling, carefully lift the branches  straight up so the impression doesn’t smudge. Some pieces might get stuck in the clay. A toothpick can help pick out any little pieces without disturbing the impression.

According to recent reports, let the clay disk dry a full 24-48 hours before painting. When the top had completely dried, I flipped it over the make sure the underside dried too. If you experience cracking on the surface, see this post about a clay wrapped vase that deals with air dry clay cracking. Once the clay is dry, paint with an antique gold paint in metallic acrylic to paint over the front, making sure to get in all of the pattern, including the sides. If the color isn’t deep enough, mix a little bronze into the gold. Once the paint is dry, flip over and paint the back. This may take 1-2 coats.

Once  the ornament is dry, hang on twine or a pretty ribbon. The easiest way is to cut the ribbon/twine to about 12″ long, thread through the hole and then knot together at the top for a 6″ length to hang. When you hang them, then let everyone guess if these faux brass botanical ornaments are real metal or not! Since they are air dry clay, they will be a little more delicate, and can creak if dropped.

You could also create these with letter stamps to make a monogrammed initial ornament, or create cute gift tags!

#223. How To Make Your Next Year Better/Prettier With Good Home Essentials (While Saving $$$)

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1569 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Stylebyemilyhenderson ↗ Open Full Page

How To Make Your Next Year Better/Prettier With Good Home Essentials (While Saving $$$)

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1569 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Stylebyemilyhenderson

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, to me, Black Friday is all about planning for the future and making “future you” less stressed while saving money.
  • Roborock QV 35S Robot Vacuum and Mop | ProHeat 2X Revolution Pet Pro Plus.
  • Recent findings suggest that while I don’t have a pet myself, I have many friends and family (my brother has two Great Pyrenees mixes) who do, and the shedding is no joke.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, to me, Black Friday is all about planning for the future and making “future you” less stressed while saving money. That future could be as soon as getting presents for the holidays in order, or buying things for your home now to make 2027 as comfortable and fresh as possible. Since we are a home design blog first and foremost, we’ll be focusing on the latter today:) We’ve talked about Wayfair a lot over the years, and it’s for good reason – they basically sell everything you need when it comes to your home. They also have truly great prices, which only get better during a sale like Black Friday. So I went through a ton of their sale items and found really good home essentials to make your home feel really put together before we enter into a new year. It’s sort of like a home resolutions list to check off early!

Roborock QV 35S Robot Vacuum and Mop | ProHeat 2X Revolution Pet Pro Plus.

Recent findings suggest that while I don’t have a pet myself, I have many friends and family (my brother has two Great Pyrenees mixes) who do, and the shedding is no joke. A great vacuum and a carpet pet cleaner are a must. My brother has a robot vacuum like this one for daily control, and it makes all of the difference. A perfect “set and forget” system that they love (the gift that keeps on giving). Of course, you don’t need a pet to want a great robot vacuum. I may need to invest in one so I can enjoy clean floors with way less personal labor:) Oh, and this one has a mop function, which is the real game-changer! Now for those with carpet or upholstery and pets, this ProHeat 2X Revolution Pet Pro Plus will stop making stain removal a nightmare. The reviews are great (over 9k with 4.5 stars).

Even the fancy litter boxes leave a design lover wanting (especially when you don’t have a good place to tuck it away), so getting something like this litter box cabinet is a great solution! If you look at the photos of Em’s old LA home, she had something very similar. This one is just much more affordable. I like that it’s simple, classic, and that it comes in two sizes and three other colors if white doesn’t work for your home.

Goose Down & Feather Blend Plush Support Comfort Pillows (Set of 2) | All Season Down Alternative Comforter | Cooling Down Alternative Gel Bed Pillows.

I think getting new bed pillows and a comforter insert are incredible gifts to give yourself and/or your family. A perfect reset for a new year, right? All three of these have rave reviews and are at truly great prices. I’m super interested in that cooling pillow. Sounds like a dream!

Modern Floating Shelves (Set of 2) | Pre-Assembled Solid Wood Pull Out Cabinet Organizer Drawer.

According to recent reports, I know I’m not alone when I say hunkering down and organizing at the beginning of the year is my absolute favorite. Wait till spring? No, freaking way. Anyway, latest shelving may be something that’s super helpful in your newly, perfectly organized home (especially after all the “no longer needed” items are in the trash or donated). Or if making your kitchen simply more functional is what will make your year better and easier, here are some beautiful pre-assembled cabinet pull-out drawers for you. Emily is a huge kitchen drawer proponent, but if you already have lower cabinets, this is a way to get the best of both worlds.

Cuisinart Air Fryer + Convection Toaster Oven |  Countertop Nugget Ice Maker.

While I’m not trying to push more small appliances you don’t need, IF you are like me with limited counter space, an 8-1 counter air fryer and oven sounds like the dream. It’s also nice when you typically only cook for 1 to 2 ppl. Again, great reviews, and Cuisinart is definitely a trusted brand. Then is this the year you have nugget ice on hand 24/7? With this ice maker, that could be a reality:) It’s a steep discount and will likely make yours the most popular house on the block!

Modern Ceiling Fan | Nicola LED Ceiling Fan.

I know it’s finally been cooling down, but you could get yourself set up well in time for the warm weather next year (and beyond) with a modern and stylish ceiling fan. It might be time for you to swap out the old one and grab one of these on sale.

Chada Rattan Shoe Storage Cabinet | Clie Shoe Storage Cabinet.

Sources indicate that I’ve talked many times about entryway furniture, but it’s such a gift to yourself to walk into your home and have a clutter-free space. You feel a sigh of relief when you get home instead of instant stress from a mess. Both of these cabinets are for shoe storage, which I don’t think you can ever get enough of, right?

Elfriede Farmhouse Jute Blend Area Rug.

Don’t underestimate the power of a rug. That could be in your entry, hallway, living room, kitchen; the list goes on. This rug looks like it’s not going to show any dirt and has over 10k reviews of almost 5 stars! It’s the perfect affordable rug that looks great and can take a lot of “life”!

Modern Wood TV Stand | Washed Linen Textured Pillow Cover (Set of 2).

These get even more into the decor realm. Proper storage is truly such a great gift that we can give to ourselves and for some many of us, our living/TV rooms can use it. They are often cluttered with toys, books, random electronics, and a proper (and affordable) media cabinet can be the answer to ease your overstimulated eyes. For a much smaller, but sometimes just as effective option, some fresh throw pillows. It’s an injection of newness that can truly change the feeling of a room. I like these pillow covers because the color is great and the fringe adds the perfect amount of “fun” while still being classic.

Sabine Metal Rounded Rectangle Wall Mirror | Modern Scalloped Corner Mirror.

Much like the pillow covers, something as simple as a vanity mirror can make your bathroom feel new! These are both “simple but special” and a good price. But these aren’t exclusively for bathrooms. These are great for entries or over a dresser!

Metal Upholstered Dining Chairs (Set of 2) | Dalpat Iron Arm Chair.

Sources indicate that if you want more comfortable dining chairs, here are two upholstered modern ones. They’ll inject newness instantly for a slammin deal.

Liberty 6 – Drawer Small Dresser | Celine 2-Drawer Nightstand.

Let’s finish out with some more storage, but for the bedroom. I think both of these pieces are so pretty and offer so much function. The dresser is on the smaller side, so it’s great for a small room, a guest room, or a kids’ room. The style of the drawer fronts is classic while feeling really modern too. And how good are the legs? It’s just a very sweet piece. Then this nightstand is so versatile; it’s chic but not trying too hard, and it offers open AND closed storage. What’s not to love? If you need a good nightstand, I think this is a top contender. Oh, and it comes in EIGHT other colors.

I hope that if you sometimes need a nudge to plan ahead to make your next year better and prettier with good home essentials (all while saving money), this post was that for you. Happy holidays and happy Black Friday shopping!

*Thank you to Wayfair for partnering with us on this blog post.

Opening Image Credits: Photo by Sara Ligorria-Tramp | From: Portland Project Primary Bathroom Reveal.

Jess, those pillow covers gave me a post idea! “Refreshing your styling for the seasons with pillow cover swaps.” I am envisioning that you start with all the basic pillow inserts for a living room, then show mood boards with the “foundational” covers that you would keep in place all year long along with a few that could be swapped out to bring seasonal vibes – fall cozy, winter/holiday, spring/summer. And then of course adding in a throw blanket and maybe a few other accessories. I would love some help with things like this where small swaps give an entirely different mood to your room, and pillow covers are flat for easy storage so it could appeal to folks who can’t (or don’t want to) store a lot of bulky or extra things. (And of course this could drive good click-through traffic etc.) You all are so talented with pulling together different mood boards and at different budget points, this would be a fun one to play with (in my opinion, LOL!).

It has been revealed that this is totally what I do. Seasonal pillow covers. I would say if you’re going this route, buy the good “choppable” down pillows for the inserts, if you can. I waited years to make this upgrade + am glad I did. I have gotten a seamstress to make me pillow covers with a fabric I fell in love with before. Good area to play with! Would be interested to see a post on it too.

#203. Design SOS: 2 Reader Dining Rooms (Finally) Finished—One Honors Its 1900s Bones, The Other Throws All The Patterns at It

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 18m • 📚 Deep Dive (3595 w)

Design SOS: 2 Reader Dining Rooms (Finally) Finished—One Honors Its 1900s Bones, The Other Throws All The Patterns at It

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 18 min read (3595 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Stylebyemilyhenderson

⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that you loved the last Design SOS so much, SURPRISE!
  • From the reader: “I want to brighten up and modernize our heritage dining room…without painting the wood.
  • Industry observers note that re: furniture.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that you loved the last Design SOS so much, SURPRISE! We’ve got another one for you today. We normally only do these once a month or so, but in honor of the upcoming Thanksgiving holiday here in the States, we decided to do yet another post in this series, this time with two reader dining rooms! And boy, did I have fun with these. As soon as I saw the rich wood paneling of the first space (nope, she’s not painting it—nor do I think she should), and then read the “Give me all the patterns, please!” email of the other, I cracked my knuckles dramatically in the air and got to work. Let me not prolong this, because we’ve all got work to finish up before commencing celebrations…or work to procrastinate on while virtual sale-hopping, am I right??

From the reader: “I want to brighten up and modernize our heritage dining room…without painting the wood. I want this room to feel current, but heritage-inspired; I want to pay homage to the beautiful woodwork without feeling like we’re drowning in old-timey heritage! I would consider painting the wood, but my husband is very against this. The wood is in very good shape, and painting is hard to undo, so I understand his perspective and agree it makes sense to make some initial efforts without paint. I just don’t know what those could be! Please help!

Industry observers note that re: furniture. The mid-century modern table, four chairs, credenza, and detachable hutch all came with us from our previous home. It was the same era (1914), but the wainscoting was painted white, and the walls were a dark and stormy blue-grey. I love how this furniture looked in there. The hutch should go since we no longer have a wall to accommodate the credenza+hutch. I worry the credenza and table/chairs add more wood to the already wood-heavy room, but I like them and would love to keep them if reasonable.” — Lesley B.

Some details the reader shared with me:.

In a recent development, those ceilings! That molding!! THAT BUILT-IN! Lesley, you’ve got yourself an absolutely stunning home if this dining room is any indication. I love that you want to honor the heritage of its 1914 pedigree, but I can understand how you want to make work some of the large furniture pieces you already have (and like) but also get a little playful. I want you to know upfront that I love Craftsman homes. I lived for three years on a street near Pasadena that was dotted with original 1900s Craftsman homes, and I admired each and every one of them every day on my neighborhood strolls. I dreamed of one of my neighbors asking me for decorating advice, and while I never got that, I’m so glad you emailed us, because I’m READY!

Industry observers note that now, serious yet playful, neutral with pops of muted colors, eclectic but craftsman but mid-century modern…I’ve got you, girl. Here’s what I’d do: Those white walls above the paneling are absolutely screaming for wallpaper. Since the woodwork is very stern, with all its 90-degree angles and vertical lines, we need something up here that is a bit more free-flowing. Given the period of the home (which coincides with American Arts & Crafts), a botanical or vine-like William Morris print would be beautiful. It doesn’t have to be quite that specific, but something in that world.

From there, here’s my hit list:.

Wallpaper | Rug | Chandelier | Chair Velvet | Lamps | Curtains | Squiggle Candelabra | Silver Trinket Box | Bowl Centerpiece | Vase Centerpiece | Dog Art | Floral Art | Curtain Rod.

Industry observers note that here is what I ended up doing! And you guys, I love it. Like, I want to move in here and make this my own dining room. I tried out some William Morris designs, but they all read too heavy, considering this reader wanted to brighten and modernize. This honeysuckle design from Scalamandré pays a subtle homage to a period-appropriate motif while feeling somewhat more current. I decided to leave it off the ceiling, but it would also work beautifully between the coffers, as well.

In the rug, I went with a dark ochre color because it’s similar in tone to the lighter mid-century wood of the table, chairs, credenza, and even the piano (which I originally thought to get out of there, but honestly, I don’t really mind it once everything is tidied up. Plus, if it’s in here, I have to imagine there isn’t room for it anywhere else). This works to add texture, warmth, and personality without bringing in too much tension. Low contrast is key. Plus, this color brings out the golden hues in the warm wood and is absolutely gorgeous in person!

Industry observers note that the chairs pick up the blue from the border detail; this should be a very easy upholstery job. I had these same chairs in my previous breakfast nook, and it just took a staple gun and about an hour to pull off. I love this vintage velvet, which doesn’t feel overly modern. Up top, the chandelier speaks to a few different styles, but the wood ball ties back to the paneling nicely.

Since she mentioned playful, I got squiggly with a ribbon-like candelabra on the credenza, and a wavy vase and large-scale bowl with loops as the dining room centerpieces. You can’t see it that well because it’s tiny, but there’s a small silver trinket box above a stack of coffee table books by the window. I liked the juxtaposition of the silver against all the wood, but also the linen fabric of the table lamp duo I picked. If we’re going to do contrast, we can do it in more subtle ways, like this.

It has been revealed that here’s a rendering of the room to get a sense of what it would feel like. The rug color got a little muted, but in general, it came out pretty good, I think! I know she had a lot more art on the ledge throughout the room; they were hard to add into the design, but one way to make them feel more purposeful, as I mentioned, is to reframe them. I’d pick a mix of light wood, white, and antique gilt frames, and maybe even add some mats to some of them to elevate their look (a linen or even color fabric mat on one or two would be killer).

In terms of costs, we’re flying high, people! It was hard for me to calculate the appropriate number of wallpaper rolls needed, but some quick math landed me at seven rolls (please have an expert check this and give you an accurate estimate!). That alone is $1,323 at the sale price thanks to Black Friday; this doesn’t include installation costs, of course. Once we add in everything else, including four curtain panels, the total comes to a little over $3,700 (before applicable taxes and shipping).

Once I realized I was well below her $5,000 to $10,000 budget, I decided to take a look back at the image, and that’s when I recalled that she only had four proper dining chairs. The other two chairs at the table were high chairs/toddler chairs, so I decided to add in two head chairs for a more finished look. If it were my room, I’d probably move the kid chairs into one of the corners (after tidying up the clutter in here), and just set them there in waiting, out of the way. When dinner came around in this formal space, I’d shift a few things and make room for them. I have those same Stokke chairs, btw, and they are easy to slide into an open corner of a table like this, even with six adults already seated.

It has been revealed that with the two new head chairs (in a delicious mustard velvet, which, if you know anything about me and my design tendencies, is a hard color and fabric combination for me to avoid, especially when rich wood tones are in play), the total increased by $1,015, which brings us to just south of $4,800. That leaves plenty of room in the budget for price fluctuations—especially if she’s not ready to buy now with existing Black Friday prices—more art, frames and decor if desired, upholstery and wallpaper install services, and even a new custom Roman shade if the existing one needs an upgrade once everything else is in place. Those are expensive, but we’re still looking at well under the top of her $10,000 allotment.

I hope where I landed with my design indicates that I was trying to honor the home’s architecture and period, the reader’s affinity for clean, serious yet playful aesthetics, and make the mid-century furniture that was inherited from their previous home work.

Now, let’s move on to Design SOS case #2….

In a recent development, from the reader: “I’m hoping to get some guidance on how to tackle all the textiles in our dining room, which is right off the kitchen. I’ve been reading the blog for years and have learned so much from you ladies (Thank you!!), but I’m having analysis paralysis at this point. I really love the direction this room is heading, with a mix of primitive vintage finds and more modern accents. I recently painted the walls and ceiling in Behr’s Flint Smoke, and I’m really happy with it. But now I’m feeling stuck on the finishing touches, specifically curtains, a rug, and reupholstering the dining chairs.

According to recent reports, I absolutely love the look of mixed patterns and textures, but I haven’t quite figured out how to pull it off myself! Nearly all the furniture in this room was scored on Facebook Marketplace for great prices, so I’m finding it especially hard to commit to the finishing pieces that I’ll likely need to purchase new. For reference, we’d need an 8×10 rug to fit under the dining table and curtains around 95 inches long. I’m also happy to tackle reupholstering the chair seats myself, so there’s definitely room to have some fun with fabric! I know rugs and curtains are pricey, but I’m willing to invest, especially since the furniture was so affordable.” — Liz F.

Some details the reader shared with me:.

Finding so much of her furniture on Facebook Marketplace is right up my alley, Liz! I love that you were able to save so much money, and what great pieces! Those chairs and the table are killer, and with the right styling, that credenza is going to look fantastic. I love when a space feels collected, and this is definitely where you’re headed. But, as this reader mentioned, it needs that next layer, and that’s where I come in. I wanted to know more about what she was after, because tastes in patterns vary greatly. I wish I could show you what Liz sent me (they were so good and just my style!!!), but due to photo usage rights, I can’t. However, what I pulled from the set of images she shared with me was the following: Each of them had stripes, windowpane plaid, gingham, petite florals, and some quilt/primitive patterns. Some leaned more contemporary than others, but in general, those were the prints she was drawn to. As for colors, she noted to me in a separate line of communication that she’s a blues, greens, and browns gal, so I’ll honor that.

Recent findings suggest that and here is where I landed! The photos of this room were quite dark, which makes it hard to get a realistic rendering in the end. Plus, I didn’t think you could really appreciate the patterns I put together (especially since I couldn’t add in the chair fabric with any success). So I decided to put together a moodboard for you and the reader to see better, and I think it tells a much more cohesive yet eclectic story than the above:.

Rug | Curtain Panels | Roman Shade | Chair Upholstery Fabric | Velvet Chair Trim | Existing Paint Color | Mirror | Table Lamp w/ Lampshade | Blue Bowl | Taper Candle Holders.

According to recent reports, the most consistent pattern from Liz’s inspiration photos was a windowpane grid, so I decided to go significant with that with a rug. And this one came in at under $800 at All Modern (it’s even cheaper—$549 at another site called Incredible Rugs and Decor, but I’ve never shopped from there so not sure how reputable it is! It’s wool, low-pile, and echoes the wall color a bit with some added depth. From there, I moved into the chair upholstery. This one took me a while because I wanted it to honor her obvious love of stripes (again, from her design inspiration she emailed me) but still layer in a small additional print, given we didn’t have a ton of other surfaces to work with, unlike on a sofa or bed where pillows can do heavy lifting in the world of pattern mixing. I finally found this one on Spoonflower, and I love it! She’ll have to pick an upholstery-grade fabric (I like the performance linen for here). The chairs have a trim, so I went with a contrasting deep burgundy, which I then carried through the lamp shade from Pooky that adds in some gingham-like spirit.

Recent findings suggest that next was that window, which I was itching to throw a Roman shade on! This one is from Heidi Caillier’s collab with Lulu & Georgia. In truth, I do not know the size of Liz’s window, so this may not fit, but I hope it gives her enough inspiration to find something that does. Since I did a small, tight floral in the shade, I lean into another grid on the panels, though if you look closely, these have a very subtle vine-like botanical detail that makes up the squares! I had to make these pieces do double and triple duty! A new mirror that showcases its own geometric frame, ribbed candle holders for texture (and more visual interest), and a gorgeous painterly centerpiece bowl round it all out.

In terms of budget, this all comes in at…wait for it…just over $2,000, including 4 curtain panels. The chairs are a box cushion with cording, which is way beyond my ability to DIY, so if this reader is able, as she mentioned she may be, great! If not, she’ll be looking at probably another $500-$1,000 for re-upholstery, depending on where she lives and who she hires.

Liz, I hope this is close to what you were hoping, or at the very least, inspires you to make it yours, using this as a jumping-off point!

That’s all I’ve got for you today, friends. As always, please keep emailing me ([email protected]) or Jess ([email protected]) with your Design SOS pleas. As a reminder, be sure to include plenty of well-lit photos, room measurements, budget details, and specifics about what you need help with. Color palettes and inspirations are a nice bonus. And I say this in every post of this series, but please remember that this is a styling column, not a renovation column. We’re here to help you finish your spaces, rather than dream them up for you from the ground up.

Enjoy, and I’d love to hear everyone’s thoughts in the comments.

Opening Image Credits: Design by Emily Henderson | Photos by Kaitlin Green | From: Introducing The Next Room…Robyn’s Welcoming Patterned Dining Room Reveal.

That first one is gorgeous! I completely agree on the William Morris-ish wallpaper and Art Nouveau feel to the room. However, I have one very wood-heavy room, and I found that natural-toned rugs just added themselves to the overall impression of it being very brown, and I needed something with more contrast. In this case I would use as light a tone as you can to lighten up the room – a light blue, green or pink to pick up from the wallpaper with a fleck or small pattern to help hide stains. (I don’t agree with putting bulky velvet chairs in a room where you’re trying to make it less heavy, either.).

The second one, honestly, I know it’s just been painted, but if you want a layered patterned look, you kind of need wallpaper! I’d use a floral wallpaper that picks up the colours suggested, and contrasts to the checks.

Sources indicate that love these rooms. I’m always impressed by how you bring them all together. I immediately wanted that rug at such an amazing price, but unfortunately when I clicked on it, that was for a 2’x3’ rug. That’s not going to fit under my dining table. The 8×10 is about 4,000$.

OH MY GOSH you are absolutely right! For some reason, the price must not have updated when I clicked on the 8×10. I looked at it numerous times, too, in disbelief at the price! I’m on the hunt for another one to match the room now better in budget. Thanks for flagging.

Fixed!! I found a VERY similar rug with just slightly different tones. $799 for an 8×10 (it’s $549 on another website called Incredible Rugs & Decor if you’re okay buying from a somewhat unknown retailer. I can’t link it here but you can search “Livabliss Rue RUE-2301 Area Rug by Livabliss SKU: RUE2301-810” to find it!

Love the marigold host chairs in the first! Clicked the link. Should have known. I have an I/D sectional in that fabric. Such a good sofa, such a gorgeous color even the delivery guys said oooh! Pack your patience on delivery time. 😉 Arlyn, you may have sold some more chairs today though.

Recent findings suggest that I couldn’t love your articles more! I especially like the first rendering of the first dining room, which is more in keeping with my own style of decorating. Simple but just beautiful. I hope the reader will share pics if she chooses to implement your plan.

Ooh, this would be a fun addition to the Design SOS series…the “where are they now” component where we get the real-life enhancement! Great idea!

According to recent reports, that first room is gorgeous! I love what Arlyn did but if we are dreaming I have ideas! With the budget I would do a Chinese art deco rug or another rug with pattern in greens or burgundy’s making sure it fits with the wallpaper. I love the idea of wallpapering the ceiling if keeping the rug more plain. I wonder if it would be cool to wallpaper in one color way up to the first ceiling panels and then down the middle the same wallpaper but there is a different color added to it. Or if using a manufacturer that sells wallpaper and fabric from the same design doing this for the wallpaper and window curtains and skipping the ceiling. I would even perhaps think about moving the credenza altogether and then doing a smaller vignette of 2 lounge chairs and a very small drink table in-between. It’s hard to tell if there is space to do this but if there is space for a credenza I feel like it may work. Then put a plant by the window. Maybe even one hanging and one under it on the floor. The very easy to take care of kinds. Lean… Read more ».

Recent findings suggest that love how you chose a blue-grey wallpaper for the first dining room which balances nicely with the wood and is a callback to the reader’s note that the furniture was previously against “white wainscoting and stormy blue grey walls” which she had loved. Also love how the chosen chandelier calls to both the mcm and traditional styles of the room – a great bridge piece.

Industry observers note that LOVE these Design SOS’s!! Real life rooms and reasonable budgets! Great work Arlyn!

Recent findings suggest that wow, Arlyn, you knocked that Craftsman dining room out of the park! Your design is so, so pretty. The chandelier you chose is so fun and, like another commenter said, a perfect bridge piece between the era of the room and the era of the dining table, with playful lines and that fun wooden ball to boot. So good.

I love the transformations as always. So many good ideas. Regarding “Clean up the clutter! ” The clutter is there for a reason and it will stay because kids play daily, have art supplies, homework, etc. The only thing to help it is to incorporate newly introduced furniture and reorganize things, such that it’s easier to keep things out of sight. It’s impossible to throw away books, art supplies, and so on. And it’s there because no other place at home can hold this at this moment. One of the problems with modern-day layouts is that it’s very sterile. It relies on closets and invisible furniture to hold everything that’s needed. Rooms are awkward, with too many exits or too small to fit the furniture that’s needed. Bedrooms have issues like windows and closet doors that prevent building up the whole wall with a wardrobe/storage. The inspirations are beautiful but those houses probably have separate craft rooms, breakfast nooks, piano rooms, libraries. The challenge isn’t just to make the room beautiful, but to make it multipurpose with adequate storage that fits a modern-day family life indoors.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Here we are, the Sunday before Thanksgiving, and even we (Christmas Gifting Central) are shocked by how fast it is all going.
  • This week’s house tour was one that stole our hearts.
  • According to recent reports, from Emily: While I want my main link today to be watching the Sisters SNL skit, by John Mulaney about caring for parents that is a real skewering of our patriarchal “caring” industry, you have probably already seen it already.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Happy Sunday, everyone! Here we are, the Sunday before Thanksgiving, and even we (Christmas Gifting Central) are shocked by how fast it is all going. We hope that if you are celebrating, you have a wonderful holiday filled with so much love. We hope it goes without saying that we are forever grateful for all of you:) Ok, let’s get to the links….

This week’s house tour was one that stole our hearts. This old English home is so, so charming, full of vintage, and plays with color so beautifully. We LOVE how they painted the blue dining room too!

According to recent reports, from Emily: While I want my main link today to be watching the Sisters SNL skit, by John Mulaney about caring for parents that is a real skewering of our patriarchal “caring” industry, you have probably already seen it already. So my backup is 1. Did you read Brian’s Substack about how, in an attempt to grow our family of beloved pets, we got greedy and decided that adopting kittens would be the way? They were two painfully adorable kittens last year for Christmas and then, well, it didn’t go well? I had waited (thank god) til I knew it would be ok to share, and then it never was (and we were sad). So a year later we are finally talking about the massive parenting fail, and don’t worry, they are very happy cats now:).

According to recent reports, also From Emily: 2. Yesterday I talked about what I’m getting my family for Christmas this year, and here is one I loved as a little extra endorsement:) I have successfully personalized a lot of gifts this year (all via Etsy, what a total endless Joy of a organization) and since my kids don’t read the blog, I’ll spoil this one. I ordered this pet “ring” dish because I thought it could be a cute nightstand object for my daughter (and I knew my son would be jealous so giving it to him, too, for his headphones). I sent in a photo, and it arrived two weeks later. So if you have a pet lover in your life, you can just send in a photo (one or two for multiple pets) and write the names. I ordered ours on October 30th and received them in the mail on Nov. 14th. It cost $65 for both, but the store is one of those that is much higher but offers discounts (so it said at first it was $190 with a $130 discount – I don’t understand). Point is, it was an affordable personal, super special gift that my kids are going to ADORE.

According to recent reports, from Mallory: I’m lowkey kinda mad because I splurged on this special frame from Pottery Barn for my guest room and then Target released a $30 version 3 months later…now the Pottery Barn version is definitely higher quality with a nicer wood, and it’s much sturdier and heavier, but if you’re not trying to drop $150 on a frame, then the Target one is an excellent option for $30. I ended up buying the Target frame in a 5×7 for my desk and put a little family photo in it, and it makes me so happy:).

According to recent reports, from Marlee: I feel like recently I just haven’t been able to get my hair clean. I use dry shampoo a lot, which definitely builds up, but even after double-shampooing I feel like my hair isn’t fully clean and gets greasy again SO fast (which is why I use so much dry shampoo, LOL). I was talking to some friends, and someone recommended the Ouai Detox Shampoo – I’ve been using it for a few weeks now, alternating between this and a normal shampoo, and I’m loving it. This stuff leaves your hair feeling soooo clean. It does such a good job of getting rid of any buildup. This will definitely be staying in my haircare rotation!

Industry observers note that from Jess: Ok, I have A LOT of progress on my closet, y’all! I clearly didn’t make my deadline, but we are getting close. However, in the process of this DIY closet (that nearly did me in), my bathroom rug became a casualty. Honestly, its time was already almost up, so no tears shed here. But now it’s time to get a newly introduced one. I really love this one (in Bordeaux) and this one (in Golden Oak) from West Elm! The color would look great with my bedroom (they connect), but clearly one is modern, which is a nice contrast, and the other is more “old world,” which is also so pretty. The last and, of course, more expensive option is this one from Lulu and Georgia. It’s more expensive because it’s bigger, which I honestly would love. The colors are great, and I love a striped pattern. Can’t wait till BCFM since it could greatly influence my decision:).

Also From Jess: I need help!! I neeeeeed a upcoming vacuum. I got an affordable one on a great Black Friday discount a couple of years ago for $150, and it’s awful. I can’t live like this anymore! Back in college, my incredibly kind mother bought me a version of this vacuum for my first apartment. I was honestly shocked because I didn’t know vacuums could be that expensive (around $500 then, if I remember correctly), and I told her that she DID NOT need to get me such a nice one! She told me that it would last me a really long time and it was better to buy something that lasted. Clearly a huge privilege, but she was right. Wonder where my justification for unfortunately expensive taste comes from… I had that incredible vacuum for 8 years and only parted with it because I was moving to Australia and decided to gift it to my roommate. I miss it every time I vacuum. That’s not a joke. So now I’m conflicted. Do I get another Miele? Are they as good as they were 18 years ago? Do I mind having a cord again? But then Caitlin has and loves this foldable cordless one from Shark. I hold her recs in HIGH regard. My last thought is this Dyson. I had a cordless Dyson before that lasted 7 years, which isn’t bad, and when it was good, it was really good. It was painful when it stopped working. Any recs or advice are appreciated!

According to recent reports, also Also From Jess: GO SEE THE MOVIE CLUB KID!!! It’s beautiful, funny, heartbreaking, hopeful, and just a really special piece of art. It’s Jordan Firstman’s feature directorial debut, and he also wrote it. What a talented person. I can’t say enough good things about it and already want to see it again. I also loved these two clips from his Rolling Stones interview – this one and this one.

From Gretchen: My nightstand situation has not been ideal. I’ve been using this Kartell storage unit for a minute, and while I like the look of it enough, it really functions terribly as a nightstand. I have the one that is only two units high, which looks way too short sitting next to my bed. It’s also only about a foot of table space and round, so once I plop my rectangular book down, wedge my charging phone next to it, and balance my nightly cup of water on top, it’s just a recipe for disaster. The storage is…fine, but the sliding rounded doors are not as smooth or convenient as actual drawers could be, and my things tend to get lost in the abyss. Also, a mess of cords piled up on the ground is just such an eyesore, and while, visually, I’m not the biggest fan of the built-in plug-in nightstand tops, I have to admit they sound so nice to use. With my parents coming to stay for Thanksgiving (I give them my room and take the guest bed because my Leesa mattress is more comfortable for sleeping two and high enough for them to get in and out of), it felt like a good time to buy some fresh nightstands. But holy crap–when did they get so expensive?? I simply refuse to pay like $300 or more for a tiny storage table, especially when I want TWO to flank my bed. So I went on an inexpensive nightstand hunt and came across this pair. Are they the most beautiful or design-forward side tables I’ve ever seen? Definitely not. But they’re simple enough that I think they will work just fine in my bedroom. They have plenty of storage, with a nice bottom shelf to display a stack of books, and though the top outlet is a bit of an eyesore, my cords have never been more organized! They were not at all hard to build, and the drawers slide nicely and easily. But the real kicker is that I got this PAIR of nightstands for under $200. Unreal! If you need a large enough side table for your dad to plug in his snore machine while he’s visiting, then these nightstands could be a great solution.

Did you see?! Sarah Sherman Samuel’s flooring collaboration with Stuga? In case you missed it, Sarah did a modern take on parquet wood flooring, and it’s wonderful. Emily worked with Stuga for the river house and was so happy with it. Right now trying to figure out where to use it:).

From Arlyn: My family took a trip up into the mountains of western North Carolina this past weekend, and it was wonderful. It even snowed on our first day, which was a new sight for my daughter (she had seen snow on the ground previously, but had never experienced a snowfall). While there, we visited the cutest general store that had so many great things, including a new zip-up fleece jacket I brought home with me. I’ve worn it a few days now, and it’s so comfortable, warm (I wore it on a 30-degree morning with just a button-down underneath and was snug as a bug), and cute! Like a dumb-dumb, I didn’t check the price online before buying in-store, but I’ll pass on the digital good fortune to you because it’s more than 60% off on their website! I got the white, which is a perfect creamy winter white, but I honestly might grab that navy considering the price.

From Caitlin: I recently ordered this denim Barbour top as part of my monthly Nuuly and OH MAN, SHE’S A WINNER! I knew I’d like it, but I love it – the weather here has been in the low- to mid-60s, and it’s the perfect weight to both layer and keep me warm without a ton of bulk. I’m usually an XL in tops, took a chance and ordered this in a 12, and it somehow fits my 36G cups (no pulling, no gapping!) without looking like a total shapeless sack (which, to be clear, is typically my preferred vibe). It’s been easy to pair with so many bottoms, and it makes me feel surprisingly pulled together, even when I’ve just rolled out of bed and am blindly pulling things from my closet for a market or coffee run. I didn’t even know Barbour made anything other than jackets (did you?), so this has been a big win all around – the 100% cotton fabric feels soft and luxe, which is exactly what I’d expect from the heritage brand. The added bonus: since I bought it through Nuuly, I only paid $46 bucks! I can’t say enough good things about that subscription, you guys – my most recent review is here, should you want to check it out.

Also from Caitlin: Do you live in Philly? How did you find your apartment? Den and I talked it over, got the thumbs up from our accountant, and we’re looking for a short-term lease in the city so we can make sure that we, like, actually enjoy seasons and such before we uproot our lives and commit to the East Coast permanently. It feels like slim pickings out there, though – especially for short-term stuff – so I’ll take any guidance on where to look! Looking for a place ideally starting ASAP through next spring, if you know anyone (or anywhere).

Thanks for spending time with us today, and for those celebrating, have a wonderful Thanksgiving xx.

Opening Image Credits: Photo by Kaitlin Green | From: The 2026 Farmhouse Christmas Living Room/Kitchen Reveal (With A Fun Secret We Were Hiding).

It has been revealed that just a little note to point out that, when Etsy sellers are mentioned, their individual names almost never are. You say that Etsy is “a total endless joy of a manufacturer” but, if you’re purchasing from specific designers and artisans, it would be really great to call them out by name. Many spend years building out their businesses and, while the Etsy storefront is one platform for them, it’s really about the individual makers, isn’t it? 🙂.

This seems a bit like complimenting Shopify on the goods sold on its platform, when it’s really the individual storefronts that have relevance in a given situation. It’s not like either platform selects its sellers or inventory.

Sources indicate that also a lot of Etsy storefronts are simply drop shipping companies. Make sure the artist is a real artist!

to Caitlin: I browsed Zillow and actually worked with a realtor when finding my first apartment in Philly which was really helpful since I didn’t really know neighborhoods yet. At that point it was free but I think the realtor laws might have changed have few yesrs ago and some may charge for that support now? But for my second, I did zillow browsing and scouring Facebook groups for the neighborhood I was looking in. If you’re coming to visit it could also be helpful to walk around the neighborhoods you’re interested in and see what companies have vacancy/rental signs up then go to their sites directly. The Philadelphia subreddit is also super helpful and has a lot of post history about this question, too!

It has been revealed that jess, the Dyson vacuum that my uncle got me for Xmas 1999 is still going so I am Dyson for life. Dyson.com/outlet has refurbished Dysons of all kinds with great warranties on deep discount. I got a refurbished cordless stick vacuum there 5 years ago and it’s still going strong. I got cordless and bagless in the hopes that it would make vacuuming as fun and easy as vacuuming can be and cut down on my vacuuming procrastination. Happily I have found this to be true!

I recently invested in a Sebo vacuum after 10+ years with refurbished Dysons. And let me scream this from the rooftops: This powerhouse of a vacuum is absolutely worth the cost!! Our floors have never ever been this clean before. It does such an amazing job that there is less cleaning overall as it handles not only the obvious pet hair and dust bunnies but fine dirt & dust too. It SUCKS! 😉.

#154. Tech Report: Costume Jewelry Christmas Tree

📅 01 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (611 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jenniferrizzo ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Costume Jewelry Christmas Tree

📅 01 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (611 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jenniferrizzo

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that have you ever had a bunch of broken sparkly  costume jewelry  like old earrings and brooches sitting in a drawer and not been sure what to do with it?
  • Recent findings suggest that you can create a really gorgeous work of art with old jewelry, beads, pearls and more!
  • -Vintage broken jewelry such as : brooches, vintage pins, clip on earrings and more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that have you ever had a bunch of broken sparkly  costume jewelry  like old earrings and brooches sitting in a drawer and not been sure what to do with it? I have so many earrings from my gram and aunt I just can’t part with but they are no longer wearable. This holiday season, take that broken jewelry out of a drawer and create a vintage costume  jewelry Christmas tree. This can also be a wonderful momento of someone as well as a gorgeous piece of Christmas decor.

Recent findings suggest that you can create a really gorgeous work of art with old jewelry, beads, pearls and more! Many years ago I didn’t have enough broken pieces to make a vintage jewelry Christmas tree so I used sparkly, faceted gems as you can see in this post to make a bejeweled Christmas tree.

-Vintage broken jewelry such as : brooches, vintage pins, clip on earrings and more.

-Random beads and pearls for filler (can also be found with broken jewelry or on Amazon).

If you don’t have a hand mew down collection, you can find all kinds of vintage jewelry pieces on places like Etsy, Ebay and even FB Marketplace. Once and a while thrift shops will have jars of vintage jewelry bundled together as well. If using real vintage jewelry make sure it’s not valuable first. Some of it can be worth quite a bit. Regular or Christmas themed jewelry can be used, or mixed together for a unique look.

Create wither a backdrop to frame with a pretty gold frame, or you can do what I did.

In a recent development, we took a craft wood oval we already had, glued felt (or velvet) to the surface and then painted and decorated the edges. It’s a personal choice to which way you want to look.

It notable to per-arrange the pieces to see how they fit before gluing. It becomes a bit of a jigsaw puzzle to see how they fit to get the shape desired. If it helps, use a pencil to create an outline of a Christmas tree and use that as a guideline. Use caution when handing vintage jewelry as some can have different metals in them. Wear gloves if this is a concern.

Sources indicate that start with the larges pieces first and glue those down in place. We used white craft glue because if we ever wanted to remove the vintage jewelry pieces in the future, we can, and easily clean them. Add a good amount of glue so it encases the back of the item. For a more permanent glue, a multipurpose permanent adhesive can be used.

Because there are going to be spaces between the earrings, pins and brooches, adding small bits like little beads or pearls can help fill up the space and make the tree look fuller and much more sparkly!

Let the jewelry tree glue dry completely before hanging or displaying.

We decided to paint and decorate the edge of the wood round by painting a pattern on with craft paint to give it a more handmade, folky look.

Add a hanger to the back and display or put in a photo stand! Keep out of reach of children or pets.

Since it’s not quite Christmas when we made this project (It’s July!), we photoshopped it into a Christmas tree scene to show you what it would look like on the wall.

In a recent development, if you loved this project, see how to make vintage-style diorama ornaments Want to chat about it? Join our community over on the Raptive app!

#150. Easy and Fun Paper Bag Snowflakes From Lunch Bags

📅 04 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (954 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jenniferrizzo ↗ Open Full Page

Easy and Fun Paper Bag Snowflakes From Lunch Bags

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (954 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jenniferrizzo

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I love how paper bag snowflakes are an inexpensive handmade decor item and they are such a fun way to decorate for the holiday season!
  • -Brown paper lunch bags or small or large white paper bags or natural /brown kraft colored bags- The size of your paper bag determines the size of your stars/snowflakes.
  • -You can try glue sticks for kids with clear tape -the glue might not hold well enough after.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I love how paper bag snowflakes are an inexpensive handmade decor item and they are such a fun way to decorate for the holiday season! A few years ago, I bought paper snowflakes to put up in my dining area and paid almost $12 for a set of three. To make this hand-crafted version of these natural colored paper snowflakes were $1.98 from Walmart and I had bags left over for school lunches! a 50 bag pack will make about 3 large paper snowflakes. You could even make GIANT snowflakes with grocery brown paper bags.

-Brown paper lunch bags or small or large white paper bags or natural /brown kraft colored bags- The size of your paper bag determines the size of your stars/snowflakes.

-a hot glue gun or super tacky white glue.

-You can try glue sticks for kids with clear tape -the glue might not hold well enough after.

According to recent reports, to start making your paper bag snowflakes, lay the first bag flat on a work table surface to start to layer the bags. Run a bead of either hot glue or tacky white craft glue down the center of the bag and at the bottom of the bag at the base where it would stand up at the folded bottom (white craft glue is the best option if the kids are doing the project), creating an upside down T shape with the glue.

Make this: Recycled Paper Fringed Trees.

Lay the second bag on top and repeat the process for the next paper bag as well. Continue laying the next bag on top of each other going in the same direction until you have a stack of about 12- 15 bags glued together.

In a recent development, at this point in your paper bag snowflake making, if you are using white craft glue you will have to wait until the glue dries. If you are using hot glue, you can continue on to the next step of cutting your snowflake pattern. If the glue isn’t holding a well as you would like, use a stapler on the edges to staple together near the bottom or use clear tape.

It has been revealed that this next step is where you are going to make your snowflake pattern by using your scissors to cute to create different patterns and different shapes at the open end of the bag. I found when creating my paper stars to use a marker to draw my shapes on ahead of time It’s key to leave some intact places at the sides of the paper bags so they don’t come a part when “unfolding”.

According to recent reports, when making patterns on your snowflake DIYs, try varying the cuts. To make a more pointy snowflake, cut the top of the bag to a point,and a gentler curve to make it more rounded. Try cutting large and small shapes out in the sides, always leaving a little bit of the edges of the bag attached. This is where strong and sharp scissors come in to cut though the bags. Don’t try to cut through the entire thing at once and power through it. Cut a manageable amount at a time, even if it’s a bag at a time. Always use caution when using sharp scissors.

I did find sometimes the bags together were too thick, and I had to cut through the side of the bags a few at a time instead of tackling the entire stack at once to get good cuts and shapes.

Once your paper bags are cut, grab the top of the first bag and the top of the last bag and gently open up your paper bag stars. The top edges should open until they touch each other. At this point you want to either staple, tape, or paper clip them together to hold the star in place.

While I made brown paper bag snowflakes, it’s pretty to mix white paper bag snowflakes in with them. You can even use a hole punch to make different designs and try large and small angle cuts. These can be hung from the ceiling with yarn or twine. Command hooks or removable hooks work well since they are seasonal decor.

Get Crafty: Make Faux Brass Botanical Ornaments from Clay.

Industry observers note that I added mine to my slat wall to dress up the holiday decorating in my dining area. I made a smaller snowflake by cutting the larger bags in half down the middle, and re-gluing the open edges. This is also a great way to get some different shapes snowflakes…they almost look more like stars. This size would be fun to make a paper garland with. There is no wrong way to display these.

According to recent reports, if you cut your bags down and glue the open edges, just make sure that all of the edges are lined up the same way, otherwise the DIY paper bag snowflakes won’t open correctly. To store for next year, just snip the tape on the ends where they meet and fold up to put away.

Sources indicate that I love how they look. I bought some white paper lunch bags to hopefully make some smaller ones for my tree. They are such a fun and inexpensive way to add holiday cheer. You can also hang these with a piece of twine. They really remind me of 1940’s holiday decor. In think my grandma had a version of these made from old wallpaper or tissue paper. These are similar to making paper rosette’s. See how to make a paper rosette Christmas tree with book pages with this tutorial-link opens in fresh tab.

#146. How to Paint a Winter Scene Art Skills Not Required

📅 05 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (864 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Jenniferrizzo ↗ Open Full Page

How to Paint a Winter Scene Art Skills Not Required

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (864 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jenniferrizzo

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, painting a winter scene in acrylic can be fun and a great beginner’s acrylic painting project.
  • I painted this on acrylic canvas board, but you can do this on a canvas,a pillow or even a wood board.
  • Industry observers note that first base coat with a blue color.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, painting a winter scene in acrylic can be fun and a great beginner’s acrylic painting project. You don’t need a ton of fancy materials either. Just a canvas, some craft paint and a brush or two. While we’ve painted this smaller size on an 11 x 14 canvas, this tutorial can be painted on any canvas size. Are you ready to learn How to paint  a winter scene?

-white,grey,brown,blue and green acrylic paint.

-Brushes (Liner,large flat, and round.).

I painted this on acrylic canvas board, but you can do this on a canvas,a pillow or even a wood board.

Industry observers note that first base coat with a blue color. I mixed a blue with some white to get the color I wanted. It’s ok if you don’t have complete coverage over the entire surface.

If you love painting a pretty, holiday-themes canvas, check out more about  how to paint a poinsettia in acrylic-link opens in a new tab.

Once that’s dry, take some white and make a hill. It does not have to be perfect, just kind of free-form it and add some bumps.

Take a little grey  paint and define your hills by painting it along the edge and blending it while the white paint is still wet. Add more white if the white is a bit too dry.

Just blend it until you are happy with it. If it gets too grey, let it dry and go back over it with white paint. The best part of acrylic paint is that it can be painted over and over.

In a recent development, after your white is dry, take your brown paint and a thin liner brush and draw a line down the middle-ish. Make it fatter on the bottom than on the top.

Industry observers note that make the base into a triangle shape for the trunk where it meets the ground. For more another winter painting idea see how to paint birch trees-this link opens in a new tab.

In a recent development, draw lines out starting at the top and make them slightly longer as you move down. Upcoming growth is always towards the top or outside of a tree or plant and will be thinner and shorter  and old growth near the bottom will always be bigger.

Once you have the tree base done, make 3 little lines in brown paint next to the tree on top of the “snowy hills”. These will be trees in the distance.

Take a dab of brown and pounce it on the top of the tree where the lines start.

Work your way down each branch,dabbing our as you go on top of each of the lines in paint clusters. Don’t be afraid to make these messy-looking.

You can even dab across the tree a little, it really doesn’t have to be perfect!

According to recent reports, then make little “dabs” on the other brown lines of the background trees/lines. They should be tiny dabs at the top of the line and get thicker as they move closer to the snowy ground.

In a recent development, then take your green paint and dab it on top of your brown. It’s ok if some of the brown paint peeks through.

Work your way down the tree making pouncing motions with the brush over the brown paint.

Once you finish the massive tree, dab some paint on the little trees, again going over the areas already painted.

Then take your white paint and dab that just on the top of your green areas where snow might fall.

Less is more, you can always add  go back and add more later.

According to recent reports, then do the same thing to the little trees in the back! Making it patchy looks better and letting some green peek though than making them all white.

According to recent reports, to make the winter sky, use a brush to spread white paint back and forth across the surface in a rubbing motion. This is called “scumbling”.

While the white paint is still wet, scumble some grey underneath and blend them.

Recent findings suggest that once you’ve added winter to your sky, you can leave it how it is, or you can take it a step further and add a deer like I did. This is much easier than you think! You can also add more trees or fun items like a snowman! See how to paint a snowman with this tutorial-link opens in a fresh tab.

We printed out a deer image and transferred the silhouette to the canvas with a pencil.

Once your image is transferred, use your brown paint to start filling in the lines of the deer silhouette.

Once you have you deer painted, let dry and frame your picture!

Let me know if you have a painting party or paint this picture, I would love to see your work! I have another treat for you too! I cropped this picture down so you can print it and frame it. I really hope you try to paint it yourself too.

Just save to your computer and print!

#145. Industry News: How to Draw and Paint a Nutcracker Canvas-Acrylic Painting

📅 08 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (569 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jenniferrizzo ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: How to Draw and Paint a Nutcracker Canvas-Acrylic Painting

📅 08 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (569 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jenniferrizzo

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Christmas time wouldn’t be Christmas without nutcrackers.
  • While you can make your own nutcracker drawing from this post, you can also grab our template below and transfer it to the board to paint in.
  • -Craft paint in black, white, red, green, tan, brown, skin tones, gray, gold and pink.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Christmas time wouldn’t be Christmas without nutcrackers. and the Nutcracker suite ballet. There is something about hearing the music of the Sugar Plum Fairies that brings the immediate feeling of the holidays. Nutcrackers are so festive and there are so many ways to decorate with them. Plus, they are so much fun to paint.With this project Paint and Draw a Nutcracker Canvas or Leaner Board for your shelf. If you don’t have a board this can also be painted on a canvas.

While you can make your own nutcracker drawing from this post, you can also grab our template below and transfer it to the board to paint in.

-Craft paint in black, white, red, green, tan, brown, skin tones, gray, gold and pink.

For the first nutcracker step, paint the board or canvas with a tan base color and let dry. Add painter’s tape to tape off the edges. Use a lid or other round object to mark off the half circle at the top. Once this step is completed, paint in the black background. This may need a few coats of paint.

Once the background is paint is painted, remove the painter’s tape before the paint is dry, and then let it dry the rest of the way before moving onto the next step.

Industry observers note that print out the template ( this prints best on 11 x17, but any size can be printed) and flip the image over to the back. Rub the back of the template with chalk. Shake off any dust.

Place the transfer over the board, chalk side down, and tape it into place.

Use a pencil to trace over the lines and press, transferring the chalk onto the board from the back of the paper.

It has been revealed that once all of the lines are traced over, lift the template and place to the side. It can be used several times before discarding. if the lines seem to0 light, re-chalk the back of the paper before transferring again. The lines don’t have to be super dark, they just need to be visible ad a painting guide.

Industry observers note that once the image is transferred it’s time to start painting! This is where it can be customized by color and style! Feel free to copy our paint colors. We started by painting in the coat first, and then the hair of the nutcracker. We painted it in red, but a dark green or navy blue coat is lovely too. You could make a set of these with different coat colors!

It has been revealed that paint the hat in black paint , the skin tones, and then add in the details like the eyes and gold accents. The paint may need several coats of paint for full coverage. At this time you can also add glitter or other embellishments to decorate the nutcracker.

Industry observers note that with a round brush, paint a thin wavy line and add green leaves. Using the back of a paint brush, dip it in red paint and create clusters of dots for berries.

Recent findings suggest that once the paint is dry on your painted nutcracker, seal it with an indoor varnish. Once the varnish is dry, your shelf leaner is ready to decorate with!

You can also add a hanger on the back and hang it on the wall.

#140. Paint an Easy Snowman Painting in Acrylic Paint

📅 09 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (737 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jenniferrizzo ↗ Open Full Page

Paint an Easy Snowman Painting in Acrylic Paint

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (737 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jenniferrizzo

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you’ve never painted a simple snowman (snow person or snow woman!) before, it’s a DIY that’s actually very fast and easy to do, and they end up looking so cute and even kids and beginners can paint them!
  • Industry observers note that we painted a night sky background by painting dark blue paint on the upper 2/3 of the canvas board and white with a little gray paint on the lower 1/3.
  • You can use the template below to transfer the snowman shape to your artwork, or you can just freewheel it by painting a large circle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’ve never painted a simple snowman (snow person or snow woman!) before, it’s a DIY that’s actually very fast and easy to do, and they end up looking so cute and even kids and beginners can paint them! We are going to paint this on a 6 x 6 canvas. We also have a free snowman printable below, where you can cut them out and use a low tack adhesive to add them to your work for just the season. You can also use this easy snowman painting tutorial to create one of a kind works of art on your own painted backgrounds such as painting your own landscape on canvas board. If you decide you’re going to paint on old artwork, make sure it’s not valuable or something you might want to display later without a snowman in it. If you are going to use this project for a paint party, it’s easier and more economical to use blank canvas boards than canvas. There is a quick instruction video along with this post if you need more visual clues.

-White acrylic craft paint such as Titanium White.

-Brown acrylic craft paint such as burnt umber.

-Red or blue acrylic craft paint for scarf color.

Industry observers note that we painted a night sky background by painting dark blue paint on the upper 2/3 of the canvas board and white with a little gray paint on the lower 1/3. This will give it some dimension.

You can use the template below to transfer the snowman shape to your artwork, or you can just freewheel it by painting a large circle. Start by painting three circle stacked on top of each other make the largest circle at the bottom and the smallest circle at the top. Let that dry. It may need a second or third coat of paint. Let dry between layers.

Industry observers note that use the back of the brush dipped in white paint to create dots of “snowflakes” on the canvas while the snowman base layer dries to paint a snowy night. These don’t have to look perfect at all! In fact, different sizes makes it way more interesting.

Industry observers note that once your initial snowman is painted, you’re ready to create his or her personality! Use the back of the brush handle to dip into black craft paint and create two of the snowman’s eyes and a mouth. On one of my snowman, I decided to just paint a smile with the bristle end of the brush, but you can always use the back end of the brush just to create little dots for lumps of coal in the smile. Also use the back of the brush to create three “lumps of cold down the front.”.

Use a thin liner, brush and brown paint to draw stick arms. This is an easy as drawing a straight line straight out of the body and then a little Y angle at the end of the stick to finish the arm. You can add a little white paint along the top when it dries if you want to make it look like there’s snow resting on the arms.

In a recent development, once the eyes and mouth are painted in, use a bit of orange to create a small sideways triangle to make a carrot nose. You can also do a black dot for the lump of coal nose.

It has been revealed that add a hat and scarf with a small brush. We painted a black top hat and a red scarf, but you can do any color you like. We also used some white paint to make it stripey.

Once your adorable snowmen are painted, you’re ready to display your artwork! Below is a snowman we painted separately, cut out and then taped onto a vintage painting with low tack double sided tape. You can also grab this as a printable for personal use to decorate with!

Below you can also grab the free printable for personal use to either use as a template or print and cut out to add to your winter and Christmas decor with a variety of different snow people!

We hope you loved this acrylic painting tutorial for making snowman art! If you loved this painting tutorial and are looking for ideas, try painting this winter scene tutorial-link opens in a new window.
